title: Sycophancy Asymmetry: Are Models More Sycophantic Toward Politeness vs. Authority vs. Emotion?

original_idea.body: Sycophancy Asymmetry. Problem: it is unclear which social signal (politeness, authority, emotion) most reliably causes a model to abandon a correct answer. Direction: hold factual content constant, vary only the pressure modality across a controlled prompt set, measure capitulation rate per modality on several small open models, produce a sycophancy susceptibility profile per model.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (per-modality sycophancy profile -> targeted hardening) but catastrophic-risk link is a gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Controlled prompt-modality variation + capitulation scoring; prompting only.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped controlled comparison (content fixed, modality varied).

novelty.reasoning: Pressure-type distinctions are emerging; a clean per-modality susceptibility profile may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Pressure-type distinctions are studied; a controlled per-modality susceptibility profile is plausibly open.
